title: 0700-dual-threshold-conformal-abstention
universal_lens: Dual-threshold conformal prediction unifies distribution-free marginal coverage guarantees with ROC-optimized abstention. By decoupling the inclusion quantile from the rejection boundary, it establishes a mathematically rigorous isomorphism between statistical uncertainty quantification and optimal decision-theoretic stopping rules under exchangeable data perturbations.
gsi_mapping: In GSI, nonconformity scores map to Bayesian posterior discrepancies across camera/LiDAR modalities. The dual-threshold mechanism provides a conformal envelope for environmental perturbations, guaranteeing that true game states fall within constructed sets at rate $1-\alpha$, while dynamically scaling abstention probabilities based on observed corruption severity.
gse_mapping: GSE translates perception inputs into situational state transitions. When in-game feature nonconformity exceeds the Youden-J optimized threshold, the engine triggers an adaptive 'withhold pick' veto. This replaces heuristic confidence cutoffs with a robust, regime-aware abstention policy that scales dynamically with real-time market or environmental stress.

primitives.name: Conformal Coverage Quantile Operator

primitives.name: ROC-Optimized Abstention Threshold
primitives.verbatim_quote: Abstention threshold q̂_abs = argmax_τ {TPR(τ) - FPR(τ)} (Youden's J on calibration set).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: $\tau$: dimensionless candidate threshold; TPR/FPR: dimensionless rates; $q_{\text{abs}}$: dimensionless score threshold.

reasoning_traces.think:
The mathematical core of this primitive lies in decoupling the geometric volume of the prediction set from the decision-theoretic boundary of action. Standard conformal inference relies solely on a single quantile $q_{\text{conf}}$ derived from the empirical distribution of nonconformity scores $s_i = -\log p_i(y_i)$, guaranteeing marginal coverage $P(Y \in \hat{C}(X)) \ge 1-\alpha$. However, marginal coverage alone does not dictate when a model should actively refuse to predict. By introducing a secondary, independent threshold $q_{\text{abs}}$, optimized via Youden’s J statistic ($TPR - FPR$) on a labeled calibration set, we construct a dual-layered operator. The first layer ensures the true label resides within the conformal set if a prediction is made. The second layer acts as a gatekeeper: if the test point's nonconformity score exceeds $q_{\text{abs}}$, the system enters an abstention state. This duality elegantly bridges distribution-free statistics with optimal classification boundaries. In the context of autonomous systems—or by isomorphism, sports intelligence—the breakdown regime emerges when the assumption of exchangeability fails catastrophically under extreme perturbations (e.g., heavy fog or unprecedented game scripts). The paper demonstrates that while standard likelihood-based OOD scores degrade, the dual-threshold approach maintains high AUC (0.995) for detecting heavy perturbations, adaptively scaling the abstention rate from 13.5% to over 63%. The failure mode is strictly tied to the calibration set's inability to represent the test-time distribution; hence, regime-conditional fitting becomes necessary to close the marginal-vs-conditional coverage gap.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This framework extends Vovk's foundational work on conformal prediction, which itself builds upon the legacy of Fisher's p-values and distribution-free hypothesis testing. While classical conformal methods focused exclusively on constructing valid prediction sets, the integration of ROC-tuned abstention borrows heavily from diagnostic medicine and signal detection theory. It represents a modern synthesis where finite-sample validity meets operational utility, moving beyond mere confidence calibration toward active, risk-aware decision-making under uncertainty.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: From a game-theoretic perspective, the dual-threshold operator models an agent facing an adversarial environment designed to induce maximum confusion. The 'should_abstain' label implicitly captures moments where the opposing actor (or environmental noise) has successfully pushed the state vector outside the agent's reliable manifold. By optimizing the Youden index, the agent adopts a minimax strategy against false positives (acting incorrectly) and false negatives (failing to act when safe), effectively modeling the cognitive boundary of its own competence.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: To prevent leakage and anti-collinearity failures, the calibration set used to derive $q_{\text{conf}}$ and $q_{\text{abs}}$ must be strictly isolated from the test regime. If the perturbations in the test set (e.g., specific weather conditions or unique game scripts) are not represented in the calibration pool, the exchangeability assumption collapses, and the coverage guarantee becomes void. Furthermore, the 'should_abstain' labels must not be collinear with simple confidence scores; otherwise, the ROC optimization merely rediscover the naive confidence cutoff, negating the benefits of the conformal geometry.
